la:adj:infirmus.html:
in-firmus, a, um (post-class. infir-mis, e, ), adj.,
not strong, weak, feeble.
Lit.: viribus infirmis,: valetudo,: classis inops et infirma,: valetudo infirmissima,. —Hence, infirm, indisposed, sick: sum admodum infirmus,; : pecus,i. e. sheep,: lumen solis,weak, feeble,: infirmior est panis ex polline,less nourishing,: infirmissimus cibarius panis,: saporis vinum,: infirmissimae arbores,: nervi,weak,: civitas exigua et infirma,.—With ad: infirmi ad resistendum,: infirmior ad haec omnia,.—With adversus: fama, infirmissimum adversus viros fortes telum,.— In neutr. pl. subst.: infirma, ōrum, the weak parts: lineae,.—
Trop., weak in mind or character, superstitious, pusillanimous, inconstant, light-minded: tenuis atque infirmi haec animi videri,: quippe minuti Semper et infirmi est animi voluptas ultio,: sum paulo infirmior,: quorum concursu terrentur infirmiores,: homines infirmissimi,very uncertain, not to be depended on,.—Of things, of no weight or consequence, weak, trivial, inconclusive: omnino ad probandum utraque res infirma et nugatoria est,: quod apud omnes leve et infirmum est,: cautiones,: infirmiore vinculo (amicitiae) contrahi,. —Hence, advv.
Form infirmē.
Weakly, faintly, not strongly, not very: infirme animatus,. — Of speech, feebly, without vigor of expression: jejune et infirme,.—
Weak-mindedly, superstitiously: tonitrua et fulgura paulo infirmius expavescebat,. —
Form infirmĭter, weakly, feebly, without energy: infirmiter invalideque dicere,.

la:verb:infero.html:
in-fĕro, intŭli, illātum, inferre, v. a.,
to carry, bring, put, or throw into or to a place (class.); constr. with in and acc., ad, or the dat.
Lit.
With in and acc.: in equum, to bring or set upon a horse, : coronam in curiam,: Scipio lecticula in aciem inlatus,: in portum quinqueremes,; cf. ; : arma in Italiam,: bello in provinciam illato,; ; .—
With dat.: semina arvis,: fontes urbi,; cf.: pedem aliquo, to go or proceed to a place, : spolia opima templo,.—
With ad: scalas ad moenia,to set against the walls,.—
Absol.: inferri mensam secundam jussi,to be served up,: gressus,.—
To throw upon, apply to any thing; esp. of fire, to set fire to: tectis et templis ignes inferre conati sunt,to set fire to,; cf.: aliquid in ignem,.—
In partic.
To bring to a place for burial, to bury, inter: ne quis sepulcra deleat, neve alienum inferat,: reliquias ejus majorum tumulis inferri jussit,.—
To furnish, pay (a tribute or tax): tributum alicui,: vicesimam,: septingenta milia aerario inferenda,.—
To give in, enter (an account): sumptum civibus,: rationes falsas,: rationibus,to bring into account,: aliquid in rationes,.—
Milit.: signa (arma) in hostem, or hosti, to bear the standards against the enemy, to attack, make an attack upon: conversa signa in hostes inferre,to wheel about and attack,; ; ; saep. with dat.: trepidantibus inferunt signa Romani,; ; : signa patriae urbi,; ; so, inferre arma,: pedem,to advance, attack,; so, gradum: gradum acrius intulere Romani,: bellum alicui,to make war upon, to wage war against,: bellum Italiae,: bellum contra patriam,: arma,to begin a war, commence hostilities,.—
Se, to betake one's self to, repair to, go into, enter, esp. with the accessory notion of haste and rapidity.— With dat.: visa vi quadam sua inferunt sese hominibus noscitanda, present, offer themselves, : lucus erat, quo se Numa sine arbitris inferebat,: se foribus,: se flammae,.—With a play upon I. β, supra: me inferre Veneri vovi jam jentaculum (cf. the context),.—With in and acc.: se in periculum capitis atque in vitae discrimen, to rush upon, expose one's self to, : cum se in mediam contionem intulisset,; ; ; 24, 16, 1 al. — Absol.: viden' ignavum, ut se inferat!how he struts! how proudly he walks!: ut magnifice infert sese,: atque etiam se ipse inferebat,presented himself, came unbidden,; ; ; ; ; —

In gen., to bring forward, introduce; to produce, make, excite, occasion, cause, inflict: in re severa delicatum aliquem inferre sermonem,: mentionem,to make mention, to mention,: spem alicui,: quam maximum terrorem hostibus,: alicui injuriam,; ; cf.: injuriis in socios nostros inferendis,: calamitatem,: turpitudines,: crimen proditionis alicui,: periculum civibus,: probrum castis, labem integris, infamiam bonis,: moram et impedimentum alicui rei,: mortem alicui per scelus,: pestilentiam agris,: vim vitae suae, to lay violent hands upon one's self, : vim et manus alicui,: vim alicui,; ; : vulnera hostibus,to give wounds to, to wound,: delectari criminibus inferendis,: litem capitis in aliquem,: alicui crimen proditionis,: judicium, to judge (post-class.), : prima peregrinos obscena pecunia mores intulit,. —
In partic., to conclude, infer, draw an inference, ; .

la:adj:infinitus.html:
in-fīnītus, a, um, adj.,
not enclosed within boundaries, boundless, unlimited.
Lit.: quod finitum est habet extremum ... nihil igitur cum habeat extremum, infinitum sit necesse est,: aër, materia,: imperium,: potestas, id: Agr. 2, 13, 33; : magnitudines infinitissimae, Boëth. . — Subst.: infī-nītum, i, n., boundless space, the infinite: ex infinito coorta,.—
Transf.
Without end, endless, infinite: altitudo,: spes,: odium,: labor,: licentia,: imperium,, § 213: potestas,: occupationes,: pretium,immoderate,: sin cuipiam nimis infinitum videtur,too prolix,. — Subst.: infīnītum, i, n., an infinitude, an endless amount or number: infinitum auri,: ad or in infinitum, to infinity, without end: haec (ars statuaria) ad infinitum effloruit,: crescere,: durescere,: sectio in infinitum,: ne in infinitum abeamus,: infinitum quantum,beyond all measure, exceedingly, extraordinarily,, n. 3, § 277: infinito plus or magis,infinitely more, far more,; .—
Innumerable, countless: multitudo librorum,: multitudo,: causarum varietas,; : legum infinita multitudo,: numerus annorum,: pietatis exempla,: pecunia ex infinitis rapinis, Auct. B. Alex. 64, 4; ; ; —
Indefinite.
In gen.: infinitior distributio, where no person or time is mentioned or implied, : quaestio,: res,: conexa,indefinite conclusions,.—Adv.: in infinito,to infinity, everywhere, at pleasure,; .—
In gram.: verbum,i. e. the infinitive,; also absol., and 8: articulus,an indefinite pronoun,; Müll.: vocabula, appellative nouns (as vir, mulier), ib. § 80.— Adv.
infīnītē.
Without bounds, without end, infinitely: ne infinite feratur ut flumen oratio,: concupiscere,excessively,: dividere,: perorare,without cessation, constantly,—
Indefinitely, in general: referre de re publica,.—
in-fīnītō (rare), immensely, vastly: magis delectare,: magis flexa sunt,: plus cogitare,: infinito praestare,.

la:adj:inferus.html:
infĕrus, a, um (ante-class. collat. form of the
nom. sing. infer: ubi super inferque vicinus permittet,), adj.
cf. Sanscr. adh-aras, adh-amas, the lower, lowest; and Lat. infra
, that is below, underneath, lower; opp. superus.
Posit.
In gen.: inferus an superus tibi fert Deus funera, Liv. Andr. ap. P.; cf.: Di Deaeque superi atque inferi,; ; cf. also: ut ex tam alto dignitatis gradu ad superos videantur deos potius quam ad inferos pervenisse,: limen superum inferumque salve,: ut omnia supera, infera, prima, ultima, media videremus,: loca,the lower parts,: fulmina,that come out of the ground,: aqua, that falls down, rain-water, Varr. ap. : mare inferum, the Lower, i. e. the Tuscan Sea (opp. mare superum, the Upper or Adriatic Sea), ; ; ; et saep. also without mare: navigatio infero,upon the Tuscan Sea,.—
In partic., underground, belonging to the Lower World: infĕri, ōrum, m. (gen. inferūm for inferorum, Varr. ap. ; Sen. de Ira, 2, 35), the inhabitants of the infernal regions, the dead: triceps apud inferos Cerberus,: si ab inferis exsistat rex Hiero,were to rise from the dead,: si salvi esse velint, Sulla sit iis ab inferis excitandus,to be raised from the dead,: inferorum animas elicere,: ad inferos poenas parricidii luere,in the infernal regions,: ab inferis excitare aliquem,i. e. to quote the words of one deceased,; .
Comp.: infĕrĭor, ius, lower in situation or place.
Lit.: spatium,: locus,: pars,: ex inferiore loco dicere, from below (opp. ex superiore loco, from the tribunal), ; cf. superus, II. A.: onerosa suo pondere in inferius feruntur,downwards,: scriptura,.—Plur. subst.: infĕrĭōres, um, m., the people of the lower part of the city, Auct. B. Alex. 6, 3. —
Trop.
Subsequent, later, latter, in time or succession: erant inferiores quam illorum aetas, qui, etc.,lived later, were younger,; cf.: aetate inferiores paulo quam Iulius, etc.,; and: inferioris aetatis esse,: inferiores quinque dies,the latter, Müll. —
Inferior in quality, rank, or number.
With abl. specif.: voluptatibus erant inferiores, nec pecuniis ferme superiores,: inferior fortunā,: dignitate, auctoritate, existimatione, gratia non inferior, quam qui umquam fuerunt amplissimi,: inferiores animo,: quemadmodum causa inferior, dicendo fieri superior posset,: erat multo inferior navium numero Brutus,. — With abl.: ut humanos casus virtute inferiores putes,.—
With in and abl.: in jure civili non inferior, quam magister fuit,.—
Absol.: inferiores extollere,; cf. § 71: invident homines maxime paribus aut inferioribus,; cf.: indignum est, a pari vinci aut superiore, indignius ab inferiore atque humiliore,: supplices inferioresque,: ordines,: crudelis in inferiores,: non inferiora secutus,naught inferior,.
Sup. in two forms: infĭmus (or infŭmus) and īmus.
Form infimus (infumus), a, um, lowest, last (= imus; but where the lowest of several objects is referred to, infimus is used,; ; v. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 588).
Lit.: stabiliendi causa singuli ab infimo solo pedes terra exculcabantur,: ab infimis radicibus montis,; : cum scripsissem haec infima,: ab infima ara,from the lowest part of the altar,; cf.: sub infimo colle,the foot,. — Subst.: infĭmum, i, n., the lowest part, bottom, in the phrase: ab infimo,from below, at the bottom,: collis erat leniter ab infimo acclivis, (for which, ab imo; v. below, B. 1.): stipites demissi et ab infimo revincti,; cf. ; ; so, ad infimum,at the bottom,: collis passus circiter CC. infimus apertus,at the bottom,.—
Trop., lowest, meanest, basest in quality or rank: infima faex populi,; cf.: condicio servorum,: infimo loco natus,: summos cum infimis pari jure retinebat,: humilitas natalium,: preces,the most humble,; . — Hence, infĭmē, adv., only trop., at the bottom (late Lat.): quid summe est, quid infime,. —
Form imus, a, um, the lowest, deepest, last ( = infimus; but when opp. to summus, to express a whole from end to end, imus is used; v. ; ; ; ; ; cf. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 588).
Lit.: ab imis unguibus usque ad verticem summum,: terra ima sede semper haeret,: fundo in imo,at the very bottom,: vox, the deepest bass (opp. vox summa, the treble), ; : conviva,that reclines at the bottom,; : ad imam quercum,at the foot of the oak,: in aure ima,at the bottom of the ear,. — As substt.
Plur.: īmi, ōrum, m., the lowest, most humble: aequalis ad maximos imosque pervenit clementiae tuae admiratio,: pacis et armorum superis imisque deorum Arbiter,. —
īmum, i, n., the bottom, depth, low

est part.Lit.: ab imo ad summum,: locus erat paulatim ab imo acclivis, (for which, ab infimo; v. above, A. 1.); so, tigna paulum ab imo praeacuta,: suspirare ab imo,to fetch a deep sigh,: (aures) instabiles imo facit,at the bottom. at their roots,: aquae perspicuae imo,down to the bottom,. — Plur.: ima summis mutare,to turn the lowest into the highest,; : ima,the under world,.—With gen.: ima maris,the bottom of the sea,: ima montis,the foot of a mountain,.—

Trop., with respect to time or order, the last (mostly poet.): mensis,.—Hence, subst.: īmum, i, n., the last, the end: nihil nostrā intersit an ab summo an ab imo nomina dicere incipiamus,: si quid inexpertum scaenae committis ... servetur ad imum,till the last, to the end,: dormiet in lucem ... ad imum Threx erit,at last,.

infrā
infer, inferă, sc. parte
, adv. and prep.
Adv., on the under side, below, underneath.
Lit.: infra nihil est nisi mortale ... supra Lunam sunt aeterna omnia,: in occipitio et infra, qua summa vertebra, etc.,— With quam: ipsius autem partes eae, quae sunt infra quam id quod devoratur, dilatantur,; : si infra, quam rami fuere, praecidatur,.— Absol., of the lower world: non seges est infra,there is no sowing down below,.—Of a following place in a writing, below: earum exemplum infra scripsi,; ; .— Comp.: inferius, lower, farther down: altius egressus caelestia tecta cremabis. inferius terras,: currere,: inferius, quam collo pectora subsunt,.—
Trop.
Below, beneath, in value or esteem: liberos ejus ut multum infra despectare,.— Comp., lower, farther down: persequi,: virtutem non flamma, non ruina inferius adducet. : quae praeterire, quam inferius exsequi tutius duximus,—
Farther along the coast: onerariae duae ... paulo infra delatae sunt,.—
Later in time: quid quod Ciceronis temporibus paulumque infra ... geminabatur,.
Prep. with acc., below, under.
Lit.: ad mare infra oppidum exspectabat,: infra mortuos amandare,: infra caelum et sidera nox cadit,.—
Of time, later than: Homerus non infra superiorem Lycurgum fuit,. —
Of size, smaller than: uri sunt magnitudine paulo infra elephantos,.—
Of number, less than: non infra novena (ova),; .—
Trop., below, beneath in rank, honor, or esteem: quem ego infra esse infimos omnis puto homines,: res humanas despicere atque infra se positas arbitrari,: omnia infra se esse judicare,: e quo infra se et Caesarem videret et rempublicam,he despised them,: semper infra aliorum aestimationes se metientem,: infra servos cliens,: non infra speciem,not inferior in beauty,: conferant se Marii ... infra Pallantis laudes jacebunt,they will not come up to the glory of Pallas,: id quidem infra grammatici officium est,; cf. .

Lit.: aliquid in aliquod vas,: vinum reticulo aut cribro,: aliquid in nares,: sine riguis mare in salinas infundentibus,: rex Mithridates Aquilio duci capto aurum in os infudit, : animas formatae terrae,; : sibi resinam et nardum, to anoint one's self with, Auct. B. H. 33; .—
Transf.
Infundere alicui aliquid, to pour out for, to administer to, present to, lay before: alicui venenum,: alicui poculum,: jumentis hordea,: (Neroni) totam tremuli frontem pulli,.—Esp., as a medicine, to administer to a person, for a disease: (aloë) dysenteriae infunditur,: tenesmo et dysentericis,.—With abl.: clystere,.—
To wet, moisten: olivam aceto non acerrimo,: si uvam nimius imber infuderit,.—

To mix itself, mingle with any thing: cum homines humiliores in alienum ejusdem nominis infunderentur genus,; .—
Trop., to pour into, spread over, communicate, impart: orationem in aures tuas,: aliquid ejusmodi auribus ejus,: imperatoris auribus,: magorum sensibus,: per aures cantum,: vitia in civitatem,: nihil ex illius animo quod semel esset infusum, umquam effluere potuisse,: rebus lumen,: civitati detrimenta (acc. to others, infligere),.— Hence, in-fūsus, a, um, P. a., poured over or into.
Lit.: sucus infusus auribus,: cinis in aurem,: sucus per nares,: vino,drunk with wine,: infusam vomitu egerere aquam,swallowed,.—

In partic., underground, belonging to the Lower World: infĕri, ōrum, m. (gen. inferūm for inferorum, Varr. ap. ; Sen. de Ira, 2, 35), the inhabitants of the infernal regions, the dead: triceps apud inferos Cerberus,: si ab inferis exsistat rex Hiero,were to rise from the dead,: si salvi esse velint, Sulla sit iis ab inferis excitandus,to be raised from the dead,: inferorum animas elicere,: ad inferos poenas parricidii luere,in the infernal regions,: ab inferis excitare aliquem,i. e. to quote the words of one deceased,; .
Comp.: infĕrĭor, ius, lower in situation or place.
Lit.: spatium,: locus,: pars,: ex inferiore loco dicere, from below (opp. ex superiore loco, from the tribunal), ; cf. superus, II. A.: onerosa suo pondere in inferius feruntur,downwards,: scriptura,.—Plur. subst.: infĕrĭōres, um, m., the people of the lower part of the city, Auct. B. Alex. 6, 3. —
Trop.
Subsequent, later, latter, in time or succession: erant inferiores quam illorum aetas, qui, etc.,lived later, were younger,; cf.: aetate inferiores paulo quam Iulius, etc.,; and: inferioris aetatis esse,: inferiores quinque dies,the latter, Müll. —
Inferior in quality, rank, or number.
With abl. specif.: voluptatibus erant inferiores, nec pecuniis ferme superiores,: inferior fortunā,: dignitate, auctoritate, existimatione, gratia non inferior, quam qui umquam fuerunt amplissimi,: inferiores animo,: quemadmodum causa inferior, dicendo fieri superior posset,: erat multo inferior navium numero Brutus,. — With abl.: ut humanos casus virtute inferiores putes,.—

Sup. in two forms: infĭmus (or infŭmus) and īmus.
Form infimus (infumus), a, um, lowest, last (= imus; but where the lowest of several objects is referred to, infimus is used,; ; v. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 588).
Lit.: stabiliendi causa singuli ab infimo solo pedes terra exculcabantur,: ab infimis radicibus montis,; : cum scripsissem haec infima,: ab infima ara,from the lowest part of the altar,; cf.: sub infimo colle,the foot,. — Subst.: infĭmum, i, n., the lowest part, bottom, in the phrase: ab infimo,from below, at the bottom,: collis erat leniter ab infimo acclivis, (for which, ab imo; v. below, B. 1.): stipites demissi et ab infimo revincti,; cf. ; ; so, ad infimum,at the bottom,: collis passus circiter CC. infimus apertus,at the bottom,.—
Trop., lowest, meanest, basest in quality or rank: infima faex populi,; cf.: condicio servorum,: infimo loco natus,: summos cum infimis pari jure retinebat,: humilitas natalium,: preces,the most humble,; . — Hence, infĭmē, adv., only trop., at the bottom (late Lat.): quid summe est, quid infime,. —

Lit.: ab imis unguibus usque ad verticem summum,: terra ima sede semper haeret,: fundo in imo,at the very bottom,: vox, the deepest bass (opp. vox summa, the treble), ; : conviva,that reclines at the bottom,; : ad imam quercum,at the foot of the oak,: in aure ima,at the bottom of the ear,. — As substt.
Plur.: īmi, ōrum, m., the lowest, most humble: aequalis ad maximos imosque pervenit clementiae tuae admiratio,: pacis et armorum superis imisque deorum Arbiter,. —
īmum, i, n., the bottom, depth, low

est part.Lit.: ab imo ad summum,: locus erat paulatim ab imo acclivis, (for which, ab infimo; v. above, A. 1.); so, tigna paulum ab imo praeacuta,: suspirare ab imo,to fetch a deep sigh,: (aures) instabiles imo facit,at the bottom. at their roots,: aquae perspicuae imo,down to the bottom,. — Plur.: ima summis mutare,to turn the lowest into the highest,; : ima,the under world,.—With gen.: ima maris,the bottom of the sea,: ima montis,the foot of a mountain,.—

Trop., with respect to time or order, the last (mostly poet.): mensis,.—Hence, subst.: īmum, i, n., the last, the end: nihil nostrā intersit an ab summo an ab imo nomina dicere incipiamus,: si quid inexpertum scaenae committis ... servetur ad imum,till the last, to the end,: dormiet in lucem ... ad imum Threx erit,at last,.
